metadataReview.note: A Reuters chronology republished by ReliefWeb reports the battle for the separatist stronghold of Bamut and its seizure by Russian troops on 24 May 1996 after a year's fighting. That chronology confirms the end date but does not give the 10 March 1995 start, which is retained from the catalogue without independent confirmation here. The locator is the gazetteer point for Bamut village, used as a sector reference for the prolonged fighting for the village and its adjacent heights; the fetched sources do not map any position in or around it. Casualty figures quoted in the chronology are not adopted; strengths, losses and equipment are not inferred.

metadataReview.coordinateBasis: GeoNames 572706 (Bamut, feature code P.PPL; alternate names include Nizhniy Bamut and Бамут) publishes latitude 43.15986 and longitude 45.19734, rounded to [45.1973,43.1599]. OpenStreetMap place node 1539258328 (Бамут / Bamut, place=village, wikidata Q4077181) lies about 1.4 km north-east at 43.16983, 45.207268, corroborating the named village. This is a village reference; it does not locate the surrounding positions, any unit or the centre of the fighting. No accuracy radius is claimed.
